culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Scottish Outdoor Access Code: there are statutory access rights to most land and water, used responsibly. Respect the interests of others (privacy, safety, livelihoods), care for the environment (wildlife, heritage, take litter home) and take responsibility for your own actions. Follow reasonable advice from land managers.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the Scottish Government's own agency.

sources.title: What is the Scottish Outdoor Access Code?
sources.supports: three key principles (read via a search-index snapshot)

laws.rule: The Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024 lets Scottish councils charge a levy on paid overnight stays. Edinburgh's levy, the first, is 5% of the accommodation cost for up to five consecutive nights, for stays from 24 July 2026 booked or paid on or after 1 October 2025, collected by the accommodation provider.
laws.heading: Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024; City of Edinburgh Council scheme

laws.rule: Scotland's drink-drive limit is lower than the rest of the UK: 50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood (22 micrograms per 100 ml of breath).
laws.heading: Road Traffic Act 1988 (Prescribed Limit) (Scotland) Regulations 2014

laws.rule: Maeshowe Chambered Cairn is entered by guided tour only, starting at the Stenness visitor centre.

Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park: byelaws on camping and fires apply in the Camping Management Zones from March to September. In that season camping there needs a campsite booking or a permit. Outside the zones the park says wild camping is still possible under the Scottish Outdoor Access Code. The park asks campers to take litter home, to go to the toilet at least 30 metres from open water, people or buildings, and, if they plan a fire, to bring firewood and a firepit and not cut trees or move dead wood. The page names no fine.

Cairngorms National Park: from 1 April to 30 September each year, fires and barbecues are banned across the park under a fire management byelaw. The park says breaking it could bring a fine of up to GBP 500 (about A$951, RBA 30 Oct 2026). Outside those dates the park asks visitors not to light a fire anywhere, and notes the Scottish Outdoor Access Code says never to light one in woods, on peaty ground, farmland, near buildings or at high fire risk. Wild camping is permitted if done responsibly: small numbers and two or three nights at most in one place.

Scotland sets a minimum price for alcohol sold in licensed premises and shops: 65p per unit of alcohol (about A$1.24 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = GBP 0.5258). A unit is 10 ml of pure alcohol, so the government's own example is a 700 ml bottle of 40% whisky, which cannot be sold for less than GBP 18.20 (about A$34.61). The price rose from 50p to 65p in 2024. The rule is a condition of every premises and occasional licence, so it binds the seller: it limits how cheaply a drink can be sold, not what a visitor may drink.
laws.heading: Alcohol (Minimum Pricing) (Scotland) Act 2012, s.1 (inserting para 6A into Schedules 3 and 4 of the Licensing (Scotland) Act 2005)

laws.rule: Scotland gives everyone statutory access rights to most land and inland water, for recreation, for relevant education and for some commercial activity, and the right to cross land (Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003, s.1). The rights do not cover all land. s.6(1) excludes, among others: buildings and their curtilage, a house and enough adjacent land for reasonable privacy, school grounds, sports and playing fields, land where crops have been sown or are growing, land where building or quarrying works are under way, and land that members of the public were admitted to only on payment for at least 90 days a year (as defined). s.9 also excludes conduct: hunting, shooting or fishing, being responsible for a dog or other animal not under proper control, taking anything away for commercial gain, using a motorised vehicle or vessel (with a disability exception), being on a golf course for the s.1(3) purposes, and being on land in breach of a court order. Park and local byelaws can add limits (see the Cairngorms and Loch Lomond entries).
laws.heading: Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003, ss.1, 6 and 9

laws.rule: It is an offence for an adult (18 or over) to smoke in a private motor vehicle that is in a public place when a child (under 18) is in the vehicle (Smoking Prohibition (Children in Motor Vehicles) (Scotland) Act 2016, ss.1 and 4). The offence carries a fine up to level 3 on the standard scale (s.1(3)). It does not apply to a vehicle designed or adapted as living accommodation that is parked and being used as living accommodation (s.1(2)). Authorised council officers may enter and search a parked private motor vehicle to check (s.3(1)), and it is an offence to refuse to give name and address when properly asked (s.3(2)). Fixed penalties are set in the Act's schedule (s.2).
laws.heading: Smoking Prohibition (Children in Motor Vehicles) (Scotland) Act 2016, ss.1 to 4

laws.rule: Since 1 June 2025 it is an offence in Scotland to supply, offer to supply or hold for supply a single-use vape (a vape not designed to be reused, such as one that cannot be refilled or recharged). The offence is aimed at shops and other suppliers, not at a visitor using a vape. The regulations also give officers powers of entry and let them issue fixed penalty notices (regs 9 and 11).
laws.heading: Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) (Scotland) Regulations 2024 (SSI 2024/269), regs 1, 3 and 4

laws.rule: Scotland has its own fireworks rules. Adult fireworks may be used only between 18:00 and 23:00, except on four permitted nights, when the end is extended: the first day of Chinese New Year, Diwali and 31 December (to 01:00 the next morning) and 5 November (to midnight) (Fireworks (Scotland) Regulations 2004, reg 3 as amended in 2021). Selling adult fireworks is limited to 07:00 to 18:00 (reg 3A). Under the UK-wide Fireworks Regulations 2004, reg 4, a person under 18 may not possess an adult firework in a public place. The Fireworks and Pyrotechnic Articles (Scotland) Act 2022 adds a licence to buy and use fireworks (s.4) and fixed days of supply and use (ss.22 and 24); on 7 November 2026 legislation.gov.uk showed no commencement date for those sections, so they are not stated here as in force.
laws.heading: Fireworks (Scotland) Regulations 2004, regs 3 and 3A; Fireworks Regulations 2004, reg 4

layers.authority: Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority
layers.process: Camping Management Zones, made by byelaws in 2017, cover busy lochshores from 1 March to 30 September. In that season you book a campsite, or a permit for a permit area, to camp, or in some areas to stay overnight in a campervan. A permit costs GBP 4.50 per tent or vehicle per night (about A$8.56, RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = GBP 0.5258), for up to three nights in one area, booked up to four weeks ahead. It covers any spot inside the permit area, with no set pitch and no facilities. Tents: arrive from 1pm, leave by 11am. Campervans: the permit runs 7pm to 10am. From 1 October to 28 February no permit is needed. The Authority is reviewing the byelaws, with a public consultation planned for July to September 2026.

layers.authority: Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority
layers.process: The Authority's own campsites at Loch Chon, Loch Achray, Inchcailloch and Sallochy are closed from 1 October 2026 to 28 February 2027. Outside the Camping Management Zones, wild camping follows the Scottish Outdoor Access Code.
